final_candidates.decision_summary: W17 is an essential, highly conserved aromatic core residue in PsaE; introducing an uncompensated negative charge causes severe steric and electrostatic disruption to the fold.
F40 is deeply buried in the hydrophobic core, and substitution with an aspartate imposes a massive desolvation penalty that destabilizes the tertiary structure.
I33 forms key hydrophobic sheet packing; introducing an acidic side chain disrupts beta-sheet hydrogen bonding and core integrity.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 candidate mutations for targeted fold disruption are robustly identified and verified against the wild-type sequence.

history.rationale: Trp17 is a core hydrophobic residue in the beta-barrel fold; introducing a charged aspartate causes severe steric and electrostatic desolvation penalties that disrupt folding.
W17 is an essential, highly conserved core tryptophan in the PsaE beta-barrel whose substitution to Asp severely disrupts hydrophobic packing.
Phe40 is buried within the hydrophobic core of PsaE; substitution with Asp disrupts core packing and severely destabilizes the folded state.
F40 is deeply buried within the hydrophobic core, and placing a charged carboxylate here causes major electrostatic and steric destabilization.
Phe48 contributes to the hydrophobic core; introduction of a negative charge in this buried environment strongly destabilizes tertiary structure.
F48 contributes critical aromatic packing within the hydrophobic core, making an Asp substitution highly effective for fold disruption.
Ile33 is located in an internal beta-strand where mutating to a charged Asp residue disrupts hydrophobic packing and drives unfolding.
I33 sits squarely within the central beta-sheet core; introducing an Asp side chain strongly destabilizes sheet formation and tertiary collapse.
Inserting a rigid proline at Trp17 breaks the beta-strand backbone hydrogen bonding network and prevents proper fold formation.
Proline at position 17 disrupts both local backbone hydrogen bonding in the beta-sheet and aromatic core stabilization.
Phe60 participates in the C-terminal hydrophobic packing; mutation to Asp causes electrostatic repulsion and disrupts barrel assembly.
F60 provides C-terminal beta-strand hydrophobic stabilization, which Asp disrupts via desolvation penalty.
Ile37 participates in core sheet interactions; an Asp mutation creates an uncompensated buried charge that impairs folding.
Buried beta-strand core residue whose mutation to Asp prevents proper hydrophobic collapse.
Leu11 is part of the N-terminal strand packing; substituting with Asp disrupts hydrophobic interactions vital for tertiary stability.
L11 anchors the N-terminal strand into the core; introducing Asp weakens overall domain stability.
Tyr18 is a key beta-strand residue; introducing a proline disrupts secondary structure backbone dihedral angles and destabilizes folding.
Y18 immediately follows W17; a proline introduces severe backbone torsion strain in the primary beta-strand.
Leu65 in the C-terminal segment packs into the core; introduction of Asp destabilizes the fold and promotes unfolding.
L65 participates in C-terminal hydrophobic packing; charged substitution compromises fold integrity.
